note: Rewritten from the original species-level description by Ahmad (1965), the original in English; the original describes only the soldier, the measurements in mm (Table 47, 9 soldiers). Type locality Ka-Chong, Thailand, collected in March 1962 (month 3) and in several later samples from soil. Closest to setiger, from which it differs by the weaker mandibular hook, the deeper labral notch and the shorter, wider head; atypus, albipennis and sowerbyi are all larger, and minutus is smaller.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head yellow to yellowish brown, labrum white, mandibles dark reddish brown, antennae pale brown with the terminal segment whitish, pronotum, abdomen and legs milky white. Head moderately hairy, the labrum with a few long slender hairs and a few short hairs, the pronotum sparsely hairy. Head rectangular, length nearly 1.5 times the width; sides wavy; median suture distinct, extending to the middle of the head; frontal process very low, the frons gradually sloping. Labrum longer than wide, anterior margin deeply concave, the anterolateral corners extended into long, slender, gradually tapering processes. Mandibles slender, slightly asymmetrical: the left mandible slightly curved in the middle, its apex hooked and incurved; the right mandible straighter than the left, its apex slightly incurved. Postmentum arched, widest above the middle, narrowest below the middle. Antennae 14-segmented, segment 3 distinctly longer than segment 2 and slightly longer than segment 4, in some specimens segments 2, 3 and 4 subequal. Pronotum saddle-shaped, the anterior margin without a notch and the posterior margin not concave; lateral lobes distinct, narrowly rounded. Measurements of 9 soldiers (mm, mean in parentheses): head length to the lateral antennal base 1.30—1.50 (1.40), head width 0.91—1.04 (0.97), left mandible length 1.43—1.61 (1.51), postmentum length 0.54—0.65 (0.58), postmentum maximum width 0.28—0.33 (0.29), minimum width 0.20—0.23 (0.22), pronotum 0.23—0.31 (0.27) × 0.54—0.62 (0.58).
